stem:
Komal studies reproduction. Offspring resemble their parents but are not exact copies. Parents pass instructions to offspring, and small changes in those instructions can create variation.

Which claim about reproduction is correct?

options.text: Reproduction passes instructions from parents to offspring, giving resemblance, while small changes in those instructions can create variation.
Reproduction makes only exact copies, so any difference must come from a separate process.
Variation appears first and then creates the inherited instructions.
Reproduction keeps life from disappearing, so inherited instructions do not matter.

teacher.key_rationale: Inherited instructions give resemblance; small changes yield variation. Exact-copy-only drops variation. Variation does not create the instructions. Continuity still depends on those instructions.
